speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Put the dry things above the wet. It is a rule that asks no learning.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The bacon is wrapped, Mother. The bags will take it.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Here is the lavender for the linen side. Press it down by the hose. Fresh sweats, and it spoils the bacon if you set them together.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You'll make a stable think I travel for an apothecary.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: You're thin. They don't feed players, then. Give Anne the strap before thou pullest the buckle crooked.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Leave the off-side buckle to me. If thou tie it in the dark tomorrow it will work loose before thou art well on the road.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then the knot is thine. I will know it if I have to tie it again.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Tie it as I tied it. Do not improve it into a property.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Eleven days that bay has eaten grass. He will be no sweeter for a twelfth. Take the bacon anyway.
